english: The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\sin x\,\sin^{-1}x-x^{2}}{\tan x\,\tan^{-1}x-x^{2}}$ is ______.
solution: Expect the $x^{4}$ terms to cancel (a function times its inverse); expand to $x^{5}$ (L'Hopital would need six differentiations)
solution_full: Both numerator and denominator are $x^{2}+(\text{higher terms})-x^{2}$. In each product the $x^{3}$ terms of the two factors are opposite, so the $x^{4}$ terms cancel too and the first surviving term is of order $x^{6}$. L'Hopital's rule would need six differentiations of products with inverse functions, so Maclaurin series are used.

Numerator: $\sin x\,\sin^{-1}x=x^{2}+x^{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{6}-\dfrac{1}{6}\right)+x^{6}\left(\dfrac{3}{40}-\dfrac{1}{36}+\dfrac{1}{120}\right)+O(x^{8})$. With denominator $360$: $\dfrac{27-10+3}{360}=\dfrac{20}{360}=\dfrac{1}{18}$. So the numerator is $\dfrac{x^{6}}{18}+O(x^{8})$.

Denominator: $\tan x\,\tan^{-1}x=x^{2}+x^{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)+x^{6}\left(\dfrac{1}{5}-\dfrac{1}{9}+\dfrac{2}{15}\right)+O(x^{8})$. With denominator $45$: $\dfrac{9-5+6}{45}=\dfrac{10}{45}=\dfrac{2}{9}$. So the denominator is $\dfrac{2x^{6}}{9}+O(x^{8})$.
originality_note: New: a function multiplied by its own inverse function agrees with x^2 up to the x^4 term (the cubic terms are opposite), so the two differences start at x^6 and their ratio needs fifth-order series of four functions (way 4, hidden cancellation). Closest known: lim (sin^{-1}x - x)/x^3, lim (tan x - x)/x^3. Different because: the cancellation of the x^4 terms is structural and is the whole point; lower-order work gives 0/0 again.
blueprint_concepts: Taylor / Maclaurin Series Expansion: Evaluating indeterminate limits where L'Hôpital fails or becomes cumbersome.

concept_use.Taylor / Maclaurin Series Expansion: Eva: Both differences are of order x^6, so L'Hopital would need six differentiations; Maclaurin series to order 5 settle it.
concept_use.Evaluation of limit using expansion: The series of sin, sin^{-1}, tan and tan^{-1} give the x^6 coefficients 1/18 and 2/9.
